questions.q: Name the rule in «ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ» (112:2) when stopping.
questions.a: ٱللَّهُ: heavy laam (starting); ٱلصَّمَدُ: sun letter ص, and qalqalah on د at the stop.

questions.q: Audit: today's rota group recites their placement surahs to the teacher. Everyone else completes the rule map for Al-Falaq on the pupil PDF.
questions.a: Rubric scores and two targets per pupil in the portal; rule map: e.g. مِن شَرِّ ikhfa, غَاسِقٍ إِذَا izhar, حَاسِدٍ إِذَا izhar, ٱلْفَلَقِ qalqalah at stop.

questions.q: Extend: write your two targets in the portal log.
Stretch: find every noon sakinah or tanween in Al-Falaq and name its rule.
questions.a: مِن شَرِّ (113:2 to 5): ikhfa; غَاسِقٍ إِذَا (113:3) and حَاسِدٍ إِذَا (113:5): izhar.
A) Clear (izhar), no bounce. Laam is not a qalqalah letter; before ه it is said clearly.

questions.q: Think again: If you recorded yourself reciting Juz' 'Amma today, which rule would you most expect to hear slip?
questions.a: Often madd lengths, ghunnah, or a makhraj like ض or ث. An audit finds the real gaps.
